segments.text: Hi, I'm Seal, and today we're going to discuss journaling and why you should be keeping a physical journal instead of a
digital one. I've been journaling for 10 years both digitally and on [music] paper, and I think it is more important now than ever
to start analog journaling. If you're sick of the hostile digital space where your attention is a currency and your
rage is a default state, writing and journaling offers a space where you can be at peace. Ever since writing on paper became a
constant in my life, I started to have more free time that otherwise would have been spent doom scrolling.
My attention grows, giving more space for [music] activities that isn't just fun, but also really fulfilling. If
you're keen to see what it's like to be content instead of consumed, stick around. I'll show you. Guys,
I love my journal. I'm really excited to talk about this today, and I hope you'd give me the privilege to ramble a bit as to why.
First of all, having a physical journal is like being told that you have all the time and space in the world to gather
your thoughts. You can pause mid-sentence and make mistakes. There won't be a black bar blinking while you
think or an imaginary red line telling you this is a mistake. Fix it now. There are no pop-ups selling ways to improve
what you have to say, how to sound more confident, more intelligent, cuz on paper, you can learn to actually be confident,
be intelligent. It allows you to be who you are, to wield your voice as is, and hone it in your own ways at your own pace.
Secondly, writing on paper reminds us that we are free. See, you can write slanted, skip spaces, doodle
mid-sentence without needing to click or switch or scroll. There is nothing holding you back from drawing. No
limitations of only having a keyboard or the software does not support this function. On Paper, writing and drawing
can coexist in the same space. You can dictate how you want to write and where you want to write. You don't need to sit
in a place with a PowerPoint. You don't need to avoid the sun because a glare makes the screen hard to read. And you
can sit anywhere, anytime with a book and a pen in your hand, the world is your oyster. Thirdly, journaling teaches you that
your words mean something, that your thoughts and feelings matters and you don't need the world to validate it for
you. Because by existing on the page, it is already valid. You don't need some comment to tell you you're right or
thousands of likes to confirm your belief. You don't need to perform. You don't need to be more than who you are.
And at the same time, you can be whoever you want to be. Again, your thoughts matters and you don't have to be loved
to show it. It will show itself in conversations and in the safety and confidence that you have in yourself.
See, I was there when Notion came out and I kept everything in that software, like my planner, my diary, commonplace,
the links to everything, quotes, and even like full-on essays, travel plans, book reviews, right? And I
made it beautiful. I enjoyed spending the time to look for the perfect gift, to look for the perfect PNG.
And I feel like I truly did enjoy my time [music] in that space of theirs. But one day, I lost my account.
And you might be thinking, "Oh, so that's why you hate digital things." And I'm like, "No, actually no." Cuz the
funny thing is, I wasn't distraught about it. I wasn't It wasn't the end of the world for me. It held like 4 years worth of
life, in a sense. But, at the same time, losing them didn't really make me feel sad or feel like I've lost something truly
important. The same could not be said with my current journal. If I lose this baby right now or like at sometime in
the future, I think I would just like cry. I would just cry. I would actually be really sad. I think the difference
might be with the sort of information, quote unquote information, that I kept in these things. So, Notion
versus my journal. In Notion, I used to hold information. I would gather everything. And in that process, I would
lose sight of what is actually important. But with paper, I can't just copy-paste an entire essay. I have to select which
paragraphs, which sentence actually resonates with me. Cuz I'm going to handwrite everything, right? And in that
selection process, I'm subconsciously asking myself, "What matters? Why does it matter to me?" And so, what I actually put down on
the journal are the select few pieces of glass that would paint the mosaic of who I am at that point in time.
Honestly, I would recommend anyone to try journaling. Though, it would help to consider it as an experiment, especially
if you're unsure of what would work for you. And actually, yeah, you are supposed to be clueless because you're
about to set out on the journey to find out what you like, what you don't like. And remember, you have the agency to
choose what works for you. Follow your gut, right? And I think another tip that would be very, very helpful is to not
have any expectations. Don't look at something on Pinterest or someone's journal on Instagram and be like, "Oh, I
got to be like that." Or you look at my journal and be like, "Oh, I got to be like that." So that it's useful.
No, you need to figure out your own way. My current system is something that organically shaped itself as I take bits and pieces that
work and ditch the ones that doesn't. I think having this agency and critical thinking to think for yourself is really
